India's forex reserves fall $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion on gold losses | Finance News - Business Standard Home / Finance / News / India's forex reserves fall $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion on gold losses India's forex reserves fall $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion on gold losses Gold reserves declined by $4.10 billion during the week ended November 20, while total foreign exchange reserves remained $84.8 billion below their all-time high Anjali Kumari Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 11:05 PM IST Listen to This Article India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion during the week ended November 20, according to the latest data from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). The total reserves stood at $705.34 billion in the previous week ended November 13. Foreign currency assets (FCAs), the largest component of the reserves, declined by $266 million to $583.19 billion during the reported week. FCAs, expressed in dollar terms, include the effect of appreciation or depreciation of non-US currencies such as the euro, pound, and yen held in the reserves. Gold reserves declined by $4.10 billion to $94.52 billion during the reported week, while special drawing rights (SDRs) fell by $67 million to $18.45 billion. India's reserve position with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) fell by $15 million to $4.74 billion, the RBI data showed. The total reserves are now about $84.8 billion below the all-time high of $785.7 billion touched in the week ended September 4, after significant foreign currency inflows through a special concessional swap scheme for diaspora deposits. The previous week's fall of $14.21 billion had been driven mainly by revaluation losses, led by gold reserves, which declined by $6.18 billion. articles.title: Why is RBI moving gold back to India? What Russia's frozen reserves and 1991 crisis reveal
articles.text:
Why is RBI moving gold back to India? What Russia's frozen reserves and 1991 crisis reveal | Stock Market News
Why is RBI bringing back gold to India? Russia's frozen reserves, 1991 crisis offer clues (AI image) AI Quick Read The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has brought back around 60 tonnes of gold to India during April-September 2026, increasing the share of its gold reserves held domestically to nearly 84%. While the move has drawn attention amid global geopolitical tensions, the central bank has previously clarified that the decision was part of its regular reserve management process. The RBI's latest half-yearly report shows that its domestic gold holdings rose to 740.13 metric tonnes at the end of September 2026, compared with 680.05 metric tonnes at the end of March 2026. Its overall gold holdings remained unchanged at 880.52 metric tonnes. But why is the RBI bringing back gold, and how does the move relate to global developments and India's economic history? The RBI has previously said that bringing gold back to India was a decision linked to its reserve management operations and domestic storage capacity. At a press conference in June 2024, then RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das was asked whether the movement of gold was linked to geopolitical tensions and the freezing of Russian reserves. Das rejected the suggestion, explaining that the RBI had been buying gold as part of its reserve management operations. As a result, its gold holdings overseas had increased. Since India had adequate domestic storage capacity, the central bank decided to move some of the gold back. "Nothing more should be read into it," he said. This remains the central bank's stated position. However, the move has taken place at a time when geopolitical uncertainty has raised questions about the safety of financial assets held overseas. Following Russia's invasion of Ukraine i n February 2022, Western governments froze around $300 billion of Russian central bank assets held in their jurisdictions. The episode highlighted a risk associated with foreign exchange reserves held outside a country's borders. Such assets can become inaccessible if the governments controlling the jurisdictions impose restrictions. Gold, however, is different from foreign currency assets held in banks or financial institutions. Physical gold is not a liability of another government or institution. When a country stores its gold in its own vaults, it has direct physical control over the metal. This does not mean gold stored overseas is automatically at risk of being confiscated. Its safety depends on ownership rights, custody arrangements and the legal circumstances. However, the freezing of Russian reserves has made central banks more aware of the risks associated with holding assets in foreign jurisdictions. The broader argument is that keeping more gold within the country can provide an additional layer of protection during periods of geopolitical uncertainty. The RBI has not said that the Russian episode prompted its decision. But the global situation has made domestic custody of gold more important for reserve management. India's current gold strategy is a sharp contrast to the country's economic crisis in 1991, when it had to send gold overseas to raise emergency funds. At the time, India's foreign exchange reserves had fallen to a level sufficient to cover barely a week of essential imports. The country was struggling to meet its external payment obligations as the Gulf War pushed up oil prices and worsened its balance of payments situation. In May 1991, the government leased 20 tonnes of gold to the State Bank of India (SBI), which sold 18.36 tonnes in international markets under an arrangement to repurchase it. In July 1991, the RBI airlifted 46.91 tonnes of gold to the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan as collateral for a loan of around $405 million. The operation was carried out quietly and became a political controversy after reports of the gold movement emerged. The RBI later redeemed the pledged gold between September and November 1991. The situation today is very different. India now has foreign exchange reserves of more than $700 billion and is bringing gold back into domestic vaults rather than sending it abroad to secure emergency funds. RBI gold share in forex reserves falls below 14% after price correction Gold’s reserve share declined despite virtually unchanged RBI holdings, as the metal’s price fell sharply from its January record high By Sourashis Banerjee Updated - November 27, 2026 at 09:09 PM. × Share WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/data-stories/data-focus/rbi-gold-share-in-forex-reserves-falls-below-14-after-price-correction/article71750525.ece Copy RBI gold holdings remained virtually unchanged, but a sharp fall in global prices reduced gold’s share of India’s foreign exchange reserves. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto Gold’s share in India’s foreign exchange reserves has fallen below 14 per cent, reaching its lowest level since September 26, 2025, as the international price of the precious metal fell from its January 2026 peak. Businessline analysis of RBI data shows gold’s share of total foreign exchange reserves climbed from 13.57 per cent on September 26, 2025, to a peak of 19.02 per cent on January 30, 2026. It subsequently declined, falling to 13.98 per cent by November 13, 2026. This represents a 5.04 percentage-point contraction from the January peak. The physical quantity of gold held by the RBI has remained virtually unchanged. RBI data show holdings of 880.18 tonnes at end-September 2025 and 880.52 tonnes at end-September 2026, an increase of just 0.34 tonnes. The movement in global gold prices helps explain this. Spot gold rose to a record of $5,417.21 an ounce on January 28, 2026, before experiencing a sharp correction. By November 13, it had fallen to $3,884.49 an ounce. The sharp rise in gold prices in January was driven by geopolitical uncertainty, concerns about US economic policy and strong investment demand. Gold rose 14 per cent during the month, supported by 120 tonnes of global gold ETF inflows. On January 28, it touched a record high. However, the rally reversed on January 29–30 after President Donald Trump nominated Kevin Warsh as the next Federal Reserve chair. Gold received another boost in early March after the West Asia conflict escalated. Prices reached $5,322 an ounce on March 2 as investors sought safe-haven assets. However, rising crude oil prices heightened inflation concerns and reduced expectations of interest-rate cuts. Gold consequently became less attractive as a non-interest-bearing asset. The subsequent correction gathered momentum. The World Gold Council attributed March’s 11.8 per cent monthly decline to investment deleveraging, global gold ETF outflows of 84 tonnes and liquidation of speculative futures positions. Recently, rising US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar weighed on prices in September, while speculative selling, portfolio shifts toward bonds, and repricing of Federal Reserve rate expectations contributed to October’s decline. Consequently, by November 13, spot gold had fallen to $3,884.49 an ounce, nearly 28.3 per cent below its January 28 peak. With the physical quantity of RBI’s gold holdings broadly stable, this price correction has substantially reduced gold’s contribution to the overall valuation of India’s foreign exchange reserves. articles.title: How gamers are using AI and leaked files to clone Grand Theft Auto 6
articles.text:
GTA 6: The AI race to clone the world's biggest video game for PC - BBC News
Image source, Rockstar Games / Take-Two Interactive Image caption, Grand Theft Auto 6 saw record retail sales in its first full day of release, hitting $3.8bn (£2.9bn), making it the biggest entertainment launch in history Hot off its record-breaking console launch, the developer of Grand Theft Auto 6 is facing a problem – and it's one that is increasingly affecting the wider games industry. Rockstar is yet to announce an official PC version of GTA 6, but with the emergence of powerful AI tools, coders and gamers have taken matters into their own hands. The developer has typically released Grand Theft Auto on PC long after its initial console launch – 19 months later in the case of GTA 5. This time it may not have that luxury – in part because of an apparent leak of files from an Xbox development build of the game, but also due to the rapid advance of AI coding platforms. These tools are being used to recreate or adapt existing games, sometimes within days, taking away the control developers have over their products. Image source, Rockstar Image caption, Rockstar is yet to announce an official PC version of GTA 6 Barely a week after the release of GTA 6, efforts are already under way to get an unofficial version playable on PC, although some projects have faced takedown notices from the game's publisher. For some gamers, it's an exciting prospect, despite the legal questions surrounding the process. For developers, it may be a warning: if a game as big as GTA 6 can be recreated, what does that mean for everyone else? The recent wave of AI-assisted game recreation has been widely linked to Anthropic's Opus 5.5 model, released in September, and to agentic tools such as Claude Code. Mark Brown, creator of the YouTube channel Game Maker's Toolkit and whose own game Word Play was recently recreated using AI, said cloning largely took two forms: replication and reverse engineering. Replication is where someone asks an AI chatbot such as Claude or ChatGPT to build a new game based on an existing one, possibly using screenshots or a description. This, he said, was similar to "looking at a painting and making your own replica" – something which is "a very close copy, but is ultimately a new painting". It's a particular issue among smaller studios, many of whom worry that AI makes it easier for others to copy their work. When indie developers Sodoj and Marco from the studio Robotonic noticed a version of their unreleased puzzle game 204Snake appear on the free games platform Yandex with the same name, they were "appalled". "The game was essentially the exact same idea, the exact same mechanics as we had, but with the art looking a bit off," Marco told the BBC . The duo were able to issue a copyright strike to Yandex and Google to get the copy taken down, but said it only felt like a "small victory". Image source, Archive Photos via Getty Image caption, Replication is where someone asks an AI chatbot such as Claude or ChatGPT to build a new game based on an existing one The second approach – reverse engineering – involves working backwards from a finished game to understand how it was created. One way of doing this is decompilation, which attempts to turn the game's final version into something closer to its original source code. Brown compares the process to "taking a cake and somehow turning it back into the original recipe, with the exact quantities of flour, eggs, and milk used, so anyone can remake the same cake". Reverse-engineering projects have helped bring games such as Halo: Combat Evolved and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City to web browsers. A related technique, recompilation, can help adapt a game that has been reverse-engineered to run on different hardware. This is one of the methods being explored in efforts to get GTA 6 onto PC. Coders wanting to attempt this with Rockstar's latest game face a difficult task because of its sheer size and complexity. Earlier in November, Cyberleek – a hacker or group of hackers – released what they claimed to be a near-complete Xbox development build of the game. They later leaked what they claimed to be the missing .exe file needed to launch the game. It gave those working on an unofficial PC version a crucial new starting point. "Now people are using AI to try and decompile it, make a modified version that could run on PC, and compile a new version," said Brown. Image source, Rockstar North / Rockstar Games Image caption, Reverse-engineering projects have made it possible to bring full games such as Grand Theft Auto: Vice City to web browsers Since the leak, several groups have posted claims of their progress on platforms such as X, ranging from getting the game to boot up to making it run at a stable rate. One attempt seen by the BBC on X purported to have some of the game running nearly as smoothly as it does on console, albeit on a high-end PC. Accounts and sites have even sprung up to track the various attempts, excitedly sharing clips of the latest milestone passed and scoring their efforts. Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive, have not confirmed the authenticity of the leaked build, and neither has responded to the BBC's request for a statement. However, Take-Two has issued take , external down notices , external of public projects aiming to port the Xbox version to PC on platforms such as GitHub. "There are no remedies available to rectify this clear attempt to facilitate copyright infringement based upon Take-Two's copyrighted property," one notice stated. Tech Life: One hundred years of AI Laura Cress talks to game designers who say their unreleased new game was copied using AI. And Shiona McCallum reports on a new AI police chatbot. Listen on Sounds Available for over a year News of the leak has been celebrated by some gamers on Reddit, who resent having to wait for the PC release. "Why should the PC players have to wait half a year if you can develop the game in weeks as shown so far!" wrote one gamer , external . "Will be funny when the decomp runs way better than whatever Rockstar can make," said another. Christopher Dring, editor-in-chief and co-founder of The Game Business, said part of the reason why the games are often released on PCs months after consoles is that PC versions are "complex" with "different hardware configurations", as opposed to the more standardised set-up of consoles. He added there could also be a more commercial reason, as Rockstar can "have a second moment when the PC version is ready". In an interview with The Wall Street Journal , external , the chief executive of Take-Two Interactive, Strauss Zelnick, said while piracy was a "fact of life" in the entertainment business, it had until now been "less of an issue" for video games due to their "file sizes and complexity". However, Zelnick also reportedly told an investor Q&A that the company was "utterly focused on enhancing our technical defences and... legal activities appropriately". Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics Published 18 November Is reverse-engineering code legal? Dr Tommy Thompson, an AI consultant who presents the AI and Games YouTube channel, said the practice of decompilation exists in a "grey area" until it "reaches a point where copyright and intellectual property [IP] are infringed upon". He added that decompiling code could be legal within limits, such as for educational purposes, but "as soon as you attempt to use it to redistribute or repackage existing software", then this is "largely illegal". "In most cases, decompiling or recompiling code is likely to involve unauthorised use of the game IP," said Aaron Treble, a UK intellectual property lawyer for Lewis Silkin. Anyone who releases or sells a clone "will almost certainly be infringing [on copyright]", Treble added, though he said the law on AI companies' own responsibility is still evolving. Anthropic has reportedly since told Claude Code to steer away from recreating specific existing games , external , saying this would breach its usage policy. Despite this, people are continuing to work on an unofficial PC game, hoping to make it playable before Rockstar releases the official version. "Seeing as this has already affected industry giants with very deep pockets, the proverbial bear has been poked," said Brown. "We'll have to see how it reacts." articles.title: AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test
articles.text:
AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test | Expert Views - Business Standard
AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test | Expert Views - Business Standard Home / Opinion / Columns / AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test AI-assisted piracy puts Grand Theft Auto's business model to test Over 512 million units of the core games have been sold, and there are countless spin-offs too premium Every iteration of the GTA series has been cutting-edge, leveraging the best technologies of the day Devangshu Datta 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 11:39 PM IST Listen to This Article Ever since the first release in 1997, Grand Theft Auto (GTA) has been among the most popular videogames. GTA players wander around fictional landscapes, stealing cars, shooting people, and generally committing mayhem. GTA is a prime example of the products that make gaming by far the most valuable segment of the entertainment industry. It is estimated that global gaming (inclusive of hardware, live stream revenues, and advertising) will generate $560 billion in revenues in 2026. Just games (excluding hardware, streaming and ads) will generate $215 billion. For context, the global movie industry will earn a piddling $126 billion this year. A large chunk of the world’s 3.7 billion gamers play GTA. Over 512 million units of the core games have been sold, and there are countless spin-offs too. The GTA series has always been admired for its state-of-the-art quality. Every iteration of the GTA series has been cutting-edge, leveraging the best technologies of the day. Digital historians can map the evolution of the digital industry simply by the way GTA went from being 2D (two-dimensional) to 3D to HD (high-definition). It has been claimed (with more than a grain of truth) that GTA is the United Kingdom’s most successful export of the 21st century. It was developed by Scottish gamers at Rockstar North, originally an Edinburgh company, which is now the subsidiary of United States’ Rockstar Games. It has also always been controversial due to its violent, amoral storylines. Players role-play as criminals, rising through the ranks of organised crime “mobs”, with many missions and side stories. Apart from the violence and amorality, GTA has also been criticised for the demeaning ways it depicts many (not all) women characters. The game features sex-workers, “gangsters’ molls”, and realistically depicted strip clubs. The timelines range from historic, from the 1920s onwards, to fictional near-future settings. The locations are fictional in terms of names (Liberty City, San Fiero, Los Santos). But GTA is mostly set in US cities like New York, New Jersey, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Las Vegas, and Miami. London and Scottish locales also appear. The cities are rendered in granular detail using GPS, and 3D maps of real places. Scientists have taken GTA locales, and run simulations of flooding to see how they are affected by weather. The renders are that good (and scientists are that nerdy). The sixth iteration of GTA — GTA6 — released on November 19, and it has immediately led to accusations of theft and piracy. This, too, is a paradigm driven by cutting-edge technology. Rockstar has always made its money with a business model involving what many gamers consider sharp practice. First, they release a version for consoles. Then, several months later, they release a version for the personal computer (PC). Gamers who need their GTA fix end up buying it twice, or even thrice. GTA6 was released on November 19 for the Xbox Series X|S and Playstation5 (PS5/Pro) platforms, with prices ranging from €60-90 equivalent. Less than a week later, there are excellent versions available for the PC. And, these are free. Rockstar didn’t release them. Gamers and vibe coders using artificial intelligence (AI) pulled GTA6 from Xbox consoles and managed to get it to run on Windows PCs. A hacker group called Cyberleek had hacked into Rockstar, and leaked a large portion of the code for the Xbox version of the game. Xbox is a Microsoft product and runs on Windows. Gamers and vibe coders recompiled to make it run natively on high-end Windows PCs. Here’s a technical point. A console game (or any native android app for that matter) can always be run on a desktop PC by using an emulator. Emulation makes the desktop’s hardware behave like the console’s hardware (or a mobile). But it radically slows the PC down, which is a dealbreaker for a game like GTA. Instead, if the code is taken apart and recompiled, the computer needn’t throttle itself. Recompilation is essentially what the company would do to create a PC-native version. It used to take expertise, intimate coding knowledge and many man-hours. Vibe coders can now use AI to do this. There’s no official estimate of how many tokens were expended on which AI to do this recompilation. But the unofficial builds work smoothly and it’s been less than a week. Of course, there’s a high risk that these PC versions are also seeded with malware. And, of course, this is illegal. But surely you didn’t expect gamers who spend their days pretending to be mobsters to be restrained by moral considerations? articles.title: Scientists Use ‘Grand Theft Auto’ to Model the Effects of Climate Change
articles.text:
Scientists Use ‘Grand Theft Auto’ to Model the Effects of Climate Change | WIRED
Loader Save Story Save this story Comment Loader Save Story Save this story One of the most enticing features of Grand Theft Auto ( GTA ) is the incredibly well-realized worlds, especially among the most recent installments in the franchise. In this detailed rendering , researchers saw an unusual opportunity: What if these video games could be used to model the effects of the climate crisis? Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA is one of the most valuable intellectual properties in the video game industry. As of this year, the franchise has sold an estimated 465 million units worldwide, and the latest installment in the series, GTA VI , earned $3.79 billion in first-day sales. Like the recently released game—which is so detailed you can even go birding in it — GTA V is a meticulous recreation of the real world . It’s setting, Los Santos, is a fictional city inspired by Los Angeles and consists of pretty much the same topographical, urban, and coastal features of the Californian metropolis. These specs were leveraged by Paul Nörenberg, a professor at the University of Potsdam in Germany, and his colleague Hugues Lantuit of the Alfred Wegener Institute, who conducted an experiment to determine whether the video game could serve as a useful tool for projecting the severity and impact of flooding and sea-level rise under various future scenarios related to global warming. The authors of the study , published in Geoscience Communication, created a digital model based on the video game’s three-dimensional terrain maps. This allowed them to estimate which areas of Los Santos would be submerged if sea levels continue to rise . The researchers calculated these possibilities based on two climate scenarios used in the projections of the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). The first, known as RCP 2.6, assumes that countries implement effective measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming. The second, called RCP 8.5, envisions a scenario of high emissions without sufficient mitigation measures. In both cases, the authors made projections of potential climate impacts for the years 2100, 2300, and 2500, and included simulations of storm surges. The results showed that, in a high-emissions scenario and in the event of a storm surge , sea-level rise and coastal flooding could reach 5.18 meters by 2300. The model estimates that, under these conditions, 5.1 percent of Los Santos’ land area would be flooded, affecting the port, wastewater treatment facilities, and coastal energy infrastructure. Estimates for the same scenario, but for the year 2500, project that the combined water level would reach 8.22 meters and that 6.5 percent of the land area would be submerged. In contrast, under the emissions-reduction scenario, flooding would affect only 2.2 percent of the territory by 2300, without impacting major infrastructure . In a second phase, the researchers sought to verify whether the simulations based on the GTA V map could reflect what would happen in the real city. To do so, they compared the results of their model with scientific data on the areas of Los Angeles most vulnerable to flooding. The comparison revealed that the areas identified as vulnerable in the video game coincided with the three locations in the real city most likely to experience flooding: Venice Beach, Pacific Palisades, and the Port of Los Angeles. “This congruence supports the conclusion that the GTA V terrain is sufficiently faithful to real-world morphology to be scientifically meaningful,” the authors write. The researchers caution, however, that their results should not be interpreted as an exact prediction, since the GTA V model and maps do not account for all possible real-world phenomena that influence flood risk, including wave motion, beach erosion, currents, or changes in terrain . The researchers also see a benefit from using GTA V to model climate effects that extends beyond the results themselves. Not only does Los Santos look like the real world, but millions of people have spent countless hours exploring it. For the connection many have to these games, a climate model based in this simulation might feel closer to reality. Workers At GTA 6 Studio Rockstar Games Vote Overwhelmingly Against Union Recognition
The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize, however. Ritesh Shukla/Getty Images Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Rockstar Games workers in the UK have overwhelmingly voted against a union recognition effort , with three-quarters rejecting an agreement with the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union. The vote took place at the same time the company released Grand Theft Auto 6 , which smashed records as it generated $3.79 billion in pre-orders and first-day sales. Over 93 percent of Rockstar workers across offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London took part in the two-week ballot. Of those, 1,163 turned down formal recognition of their branch of the IWGB (Independent Workers Union of Great Britain), while 381 were in favor, according to IGN . The Rockstar Game Workers Union will continue to organize without a formal agreement with the company. However, the result means Rockstar management won't be obligated to officially recognize the union or hold regular meetings with representatives. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society — this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for," the union said in a statement . "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We're ready to put in the effort to make that happen." It added that it will keep battling for "pay transparency, contractual overtime pay and protections against AI and layoffs." "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 ," Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar Games head of publishing, said in a statement . "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together." Rockstar had indicated a willingness to work with its workers on unionization. "We go where the team goes," Klobe told Bloomberg for a story about the making of GTA 6 . "So if they want a union, they will have a union." In October last year, Rockstar fired dozens of workers , claiming they had shared confidential details about GTA 6 and made disparaging remarks about the company. The IWGB issued formal legal claims against Rockstar in which it accused the Take-Two subsidiary of union busting and unlawfully firing those workers. An employment tribunal heard closing evidence last week and a final judgement in the case is pending.

Proxy advisors urge Sebi intervention over related-party concerns in Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal | Company Business News Tata Steel is embarking on a very high capex spree at a time when steel margins are depressed, thus, exposing the company to financial risk, as per ICICI Securities. (File Photo: Reuters) Summary Three proxy advisory firms warn Tata Steel and APL Apollo’s complex ₹ 28,000-crore deal may breach Sebi related-party rules. They urge scrutiny, arguing the linked transactions could benefit APL Apollo’s promoters while shifting debt to public shareholders. Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Mumbai: The complex deal between Tata Steel Ltd and APL Apollo Tubes Ltd could violate the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (Sebi) related-party transaction rules, three proxy advisory firms have warned, urging the market regulator to intervene. In a two-part transaction, Tata Steel first announced the sale of two of its units to APL Apollo on Sunday evening for ₹ 28,000 crore, financed through debt. On Monday morning, the two companies announced the second leg, wherein Tata Steel would acquire a controlling stake in the tubes manufacturer by buying out its promoters and acquiring more shares in a subsequent open offer. Separately, Tata Steel and the promoters of APL Apollo also agreed to enter an exclusive contract-manufacturing arrangement following their exit from the company. By structuring the transaction in this manner, the two companies ensured that Tata Steel was not a related party of APL Apollo on Sunday evening when the tubes maker decided to buy its assets, as per proxy advisors Institutional Investor Advisory Services (IiAS), Stakeholders Empowerment Services (SES), and InGovern. Thus, they avoided the requirement of seeking shareholder approval for the transaction, which is mandatory for related-party deals, the proxy advisors said. However, such deal-engineering runs afoul of Sebi’s “purpose and effect” test, which has been applicable since April 2023, they said. According to this doctrine, a deal between a listed company and a non-related party, as in this case, could be deemed as a related-party transaction, if the purpose and effect of it is to benefit a related party of the listed company. Here, even though Tata Steel was not a related party of APL Apollo at the time the latter agreed to buy the two companies from it, the deal benefitted the promoters of APL Apollo, who were a related party, the proxy advisors argue. “The transaction must be assessed as a whole, not as three legally separate announcements. The asset sale, promoter-stake sale, open offer and SG Spectra arrangement are commercially interlinked and may collectively benefit APL Apollo’s promoter group,” InGovern argued in a report dated 25 November. IiAS called upon Sebi to determine whether the purpose-and-effect test applies in this case, and to decide whether the arrangement between Tata Steel and the Gupta family , the promoters of APL Apollo, amounted to a differential payment to two sets of investors. “APL Apollo will have to borrow heavily to buy assets from the company that is about to become its promoter, and its public shareholders will carry that debt. That outcome is hard to reconcile with what the related party rules are for, even if the timing technically keeps the deal outside their scope,” IiAS noted in a report. Approval of the minority shareholders of APL Apollo must be sought before the acquisition of the two assets of Tata Steel by APL Apollo for ₹ 28,000 crore, which is several times more than what the total assets of the buyer are worth, SES noted. APL Apollo and Sebi did not immediately respond to Mint’s request for comment. Market backlash has prompted Tata Steel top management to acknowledge growing investor concerns, saying it is evaluating whether changes to the deal structure are needed, chief executive officer and managing director T.V. Narendran said in an interview with NDTV Profit on Wednesday. “We have taken cognisance of the feedback received and are carefully examining the concerns raised to determine how best to address them,” said a Tata Steel spokesperson over email. Shares of APL Apollo have fallen more than 30% on the BSE since the deal was announced on Sunday, closing at ₹ 1,481 on Thursday. Tata Steel shares have declined a little over 8% over the same period, to ₹ 163.35. Earlier on Wednesday, investors and proxy firms slammed APL Apollo’s proposed deal with Tata Steel, calling the transaction unfair to the company’s minority shareholders, raising concerns whether the ₹ 28,000-crore deal will receive shareholder approval. The key concern lies in the complicated structuring of the deal, where APL Apollo will buy two assets from Tata Steel for a combined ₹ 28,000 crore, funded through debt. Tata Steel, in turn, will pay ₹ 15,510 crore for the 26.38% promoter stake in the tubes manufacturing company and make an open offer for another 26% stake, costing about ₹ 16,756 crore upon full subscription. articles.title: No stay for Tata Trusts: HC lets Tata Sons board meet, casting vote intact
articles.text:
No stay for Tata Trusts: HC lets Tata Sons board meet, casting vote intact | Company Business News An immediate fallout is that it clears the uncertainty on Tata Sons kickstarting its planned process to take the company in six months. ( Mint ) AI Quick Read Mumbai: The Bombay High Court on Friday allowed Tata Sons to hold its board meeting on Monday, rejecting a plea by two Tata trusts to bar the company from using a tie-breaker vote. Any decisions taken at the meeting will remain subject to the outcome of the case, which will next be heard on 21 January. “Let the meeting go on,” Justice Abhay Ahuja said after more than three hours of arguments from nine senior lawyers, including Harish Salve, Abhishek Manu Singhvi and Mukul Rohatgi. The court declined interim relief to Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and RD Tata Trust (RDTT), which together own 30.17% of Tata Sons. The trusts fear a repeat of what happened on 17 September . At that board meeting, Tata Trusts nominee Noel Tata voted against giving chairman N Chandrasekaran a fresh term, while fellow nominee Venu Srinivasan voted for it. Independent director Harish Manwani, who chaired the discussion, then used his deciding vote to approve the resolution, prompting objections from Noel. About 200 people filled the courtroom on Friday to witness one of the most closely watched corporate battles in recent memory: Tata Trusts, which owns about two-thirds of Tata Sons, suing the board of the very company it controls. The immediate effect of Friday’s order is to allow Tata Sons to proceed with its planned steps towards becoming a public company within six months, despite opposition from Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata. However, any board decision on Monday, including a move to call an extraordinary general meeting (EGM), will remain subject to the court’s final order, an executive aware of the matter said. “There is a possibility that the manner of voting at the earlier board meeting may be replicated, which would affect Tata Trusts’ interests. However, the fact that the decisions will be subject to the Bombay High Court’s order would offer some relief,” said Gaurav Pingle, a partner at Pune-based corporate law firm Forefront Legal Consulting LLP. Friday’s ruling is a win for Tata Sons, but a conditional one, according to an executive privy to the developments. Any resolution passed by the board, including steps towards a public listing, could be set aside if the Trusts succeed in the case in January, the executive said. Tata Sons’ agenda for Monday includes a proposal to call an EGM, following the RBI’s letters dated 11 September and 16 November. At the meeting, the company wants to put two resolutions before shareholders: the reappointment of Chandrasekaran for a third five-year term and the steps required to take Tata Sons public. The Trusts contend that the tie-breaking vote violated Article 121 of Tata Sons’ articles of association, which they say requires a majority of their nominee directors to vote in favour of a resolution. “A majority of two is two and not one,” Tata Trusts had said in September. Their counsel cautioned on Friday that the board could use the same approach again, and that any decision taken in this manner “could not easily be reversed”. “This is a foot in the door for the Trusts,” said a second executive privy to the developments. “Simply because all decisions, including the reappointment of chairman Chandrasekaran on 17 September using the casting vote, are now conditional on the outcome of this case.” Tata Trusts’ counsel Abhishek Manu Singhvi argued that the articles of association give a majority of the Trusts’ nominee directors the right to an affirmative vote before a matter proceeds to a subsequent board vote. At the 17 September meeting, when the two nominees—Noel Tata and Venu Srinivasan—failed to reach a consensus, a majority was not achieved. As a result, the resolution to reappoint Chandrasekaran for another term did not receive the required affirmative vote, he argued. Manwani, therefore, could not cast a deciding vote when the nominee directors had not reached a majority, Singhvi said. The resolution had failed once the affirmative vote was absent, he argued. Tata Sons ’ counsel Harish Salve said the situation had been created by the Trusts themselves. They had nominated two directors, leading to a deadlock between them, he argued. Tata Sons’ rules allow for a board of between five and 15 members, and the Trusts had never suggested appointing more nominees, which could have given them a larger representation on the board, Salve said. “Who created this problem? The trustees did. They cannot now convert Article 121 from saying majority to unanimity,” Salve said. He added that the situation amounted to Tata Sons being held hostage by the Trusts’ nominee directors, whose inability to agree was paralysing the board’s proceedings. He accused Noel Tata of creating a situation in which only decisions he approved could be passed. Salve then listed the matters the Tata Sons board would discuss on Monday and argued that none was urgent enough to warrant postponing the meeting. On the proposed listing of Tata Sons to comply with the RBI’s directives, another point of disagreement between the Trusts and the company, Salve said the matter would come up for a shareholder vote in any case. The Trusts could use their majority to vote against it, he argued. Pausing the 30 November meeting, meanwhile, would force the company to act on Noel Tata’s terms. Senior advocate Janak Dwarkadas, representing Noel Tata, said the matter was not about Noel personally. Any nominee trustee, including Venu Srinivasan, could vote against a resolution; if the required affirmative vote was not secured, the resolution could be defeated, he argued. “We are not concerned with what they decide in the meeting,” Singhvi said. “The ground I am raising for interim [relief] is subject-neutral. It depends on an article which cuts across any subject. The article says anything which requires voting,” he said. Jensen Huang's return did little to ease AI jitters. We bought on weakness Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Stocks advanced over the holiday-shortened trading week, but it was far from smooth sailing. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite advanced 6.6% for the week, while the S & P 500 gained 5.6% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 5.5%. The gains were driven by Monday's surge, when the Nasdaq and S & P 500 posted their best sessions since April 2025 — up 6.35% and 4.73% , respectively — after Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO. But the relief rally quickly lost momentum. Selling intensified Wednesday, with the Nasdaq plunging as much as 4.6% and the Dow shedding more than 1,100 points at their session lows. Stocks staged a dramatic comeback as the session progressed, with the Dow turning positive and the Nasdaq and S & P 500 paring much of their losses, though the two remained in negative territory as AI stocks continued to struggle. A worsening macroeconomic backdrop also weighed on investor sentiment. Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures price index report showed annual inflation accelerating to 3.8% in October, nearly twice the Federal Reserve's 2% target, while core inflation came in hotter than expected at 3.3%. The data, coupled with the Trump administration's announcement of new tariffs on more than a dozen major trading partners, heightened concerns about further Federal Reserve rate hikes. The CME FedWatch tool indicates a 98% chance of a quarter-point hike at the December meeting, up from 93.5% a week ago. Stocks bounced back on Friday, with technology stocks once again taking the lead. Here's a closer look at the three things that shaped our portfolio. Huang's back, but AI jitters remain Jensen Huang's stunning reinstatement as Nvidia CEO on Monday lifted a major overhang on the chipmaker and temporarily reignited the AI trade. President Donald Trump told CNBC he intervened directly with Nvidia's board to bring Huang back, underscoring the CEO's importance to U.S. national interests. Nvidia shares soared more than 31% Monday, erasing nearly all their losses following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid an affair scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy. The news fueled the Nasdaq and S & P 500's best sessions since April 2025. "Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one company," Jim said Monday on " Mad Money ." "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary." Jim argued that Huang's return warrants a higher valuation for Nvidia. He said the stock deserves to trade at roughly 12 times earnings, putting his price target at $199. Still, headwinds remain, including political opposition to data center construction, uncertainty over chip sales to China and a more hawkish Fed. The relief rally proved short-lived , with chip stocks coming under renewed pressure Tuesday and Wednesday and Anthropic even falling below its $83 IPO price. Shares of Nvidia slipped roughly 5.9% on Tuesday and another 4% on Wednesday . Huang's return removed a major source of uncertainty, but the broader AI trade is hardly out of the woods. CrowdStrike's $44 billion bet CrowdStrike announced Monday that it would acquire Zscaler for roughly $44 billion in an all-stock deal, marking its largest acquisition to date and the latest major consolidation in the cybersecurity industry. CrowdStrike shares fell roughly 9% on Monday, ending the week as the worst performer in our portfolio amid concerns about shareholder dilution that overshadowed the company's better-than-expected quarterly results. Shares of Zscaler rose more than 17% on Monday. Strategically, the acquisition fills a significant gap in CrowdStrike's cybersecurity offerings. While its Falcon platform protects devices and cloud systems, Zscaler brings network security capabilities, allowing the combined company to offer customers more comprehensive protection against increasingly sophisticated AI-powered attacks. In an interview with Jim on "Mad Money," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said the acquisition expands the company's addressable market by roughly $185 billion and creates significant cross-selling opportunities, given the limited overlap between the companies' customer bases. Kurtz called the deal "a winning combination." While concerns about Google Search's ability to monetize AI-powered queries and fend off competition persist, Alphabet's valuation of just below 19 times estimated 2027 earnings presents an opportunity. Mounting political opposition to data center construction could also make Alphabet's existing AI infrastructure more valuable while easing capital spending pressures. We put more cash to work Wednesday, buying 10 shares of Goldman Sachs . That was Nvidia’s succession test, and the board failed it By Andrea Petrone Andrea Petrone Down Arrow Button Icon By Andrea Petrone Andrea Petrone Down Arrow Button Icon November 27, 2026, 7:30 AM ET Photograph by Joe Pugliese—August Google source logo Add Fortune on Google for similar content. Add us on Google Add us on Google Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia is being told as a comeback. The shares jumped about 30% on the news. The founder was back at his desk. Order restored. I read it differently. Those 11 days were the first real test of whether Nvidia could function without the man who built it. The board failed that test, and the way it failed should worry directors at every company whose CEO looks irreplaceable. The sequence of events tells a story. On November 12, Nvidia announced that its board had accepted Huang’s resignation , after reports about his private life and a foreign intelligence operation aimed at him. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO. The board said it would consider internal and external candidates. Five days later, on the earnings call, chair Harvey Jones told analysts the board did “not intend to reinstate Jensen.” Then the alternatives fell away. The Financial Times reported that the board had approached Rene Haas, the Arm CEO who spent seven years at Nvidia. On November 23, Haas extended his contract at Arm through 2033. The same day, Nvidia’s directors voted unanimously to bring Huang back, saying they had received input from senior levels of the U.S. government . Trump told CNBC that he made a personal assurance that sealed the decision. The board’s own independent investigation is still open. The directors reinstated their CEO before their own inquiry had finished. That’s the detail I can’t get past. A board that says no on a Tuesday and yes six days later has run out of options. A CEO nobody can replace is a CEO nobody can refuse. Accountability depends on a credible alternative. When a board has a successor ready, its questions carry weight, because everyone in the room knows the company survives if the answers fall short. When it has nobody, the CEO holds the leverage and both sides know it. The duty to oversee him turns into a duty to keep him. Huang has run Nvidia since he co-founded it in 1993. The board had three decades to prepare for the day he wasn’t there. When that day came, it had a CFO doing two jobs, one outside name, and a market that wanted him back. Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld wrote in Fortune the board had no Plan B. Investors made the same point from the other side. Within days of the resignation, prominent shareholders were urging the board to keep the door open to Huang. Nobody outside the company had the facts. What they were pricing was a business with no one else to run it. The board has since created a national security committee and is hiring a chief compliance officer. Those are controls on conduct. Neither one is a successor. I coach CEOs, and I’ve watched how boards arrive here. Nobody decides to skip succession. It gets postponed, one good quarter at a time. Over the years a founder’s identity and the company’s fuse. Raising the question of who comes next starts to feel like disloyalty, so directors leave it for another meeting. The CEO rarely pushes either. Planning your own exit means picturing a company that no longer needs you, and that is the hardest thing to ask of someone whose whole identity is the company. So both sides stay comfortable. The cost arrives on the one day the board needs a choice and finds it doesn’t have one. Plenty of boards are living with the same arrangement right now, and it’s invisible for as long as the results are good. Two tests will tell a director where their board stands. First, name the person who could run the company on Monday. One name, already inside the building, whom the top team would follow. If the honest answer is the CFO as caretaker, you have a holding pattern. Second, recall the last time the board said no to the CEO on something he cared about. If nobody can remember one, the board has already stopped overseeing him. It just hasn’t been tested yet. Huang may prove to be the right leader for Nvidia’s next chapter. The investigation may answer every open question. Neither would change what the 11 days showed. The board now enters the next crisis in a weaker position than the last one. It has shown its investors, its government and its CEO that it has no alternative to him. He knows it. So does everyone who will ever need to challenge him. Every director reading this should ask the question Nvidia’s board had to answer in public. If our CEO were gone tomorrow, would we have a choice? The RBI said the minimum daily maintenance of CRR by Banks will be reduced from 99 per cent of the requirement to 90 per cent. This comes in view of liquidity tightness in the banking system. The central bank had raised the minimum daily maintenance of the CRR from 90 per cent of the requirement to 99 per cent effective from the fortnight beginning October 16, 2026. The October step was necessitated as Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auctions were not proving enough to neutralise the surplus Rupee liquidity generated due to the US Dollar-Rupee Forex Swap facility that RBI provided for fresh FCNR (B) deposits mobilised by banks (from June 8 to August 31, 2026). With the latest announcement, RBI has restored the status quo on the minimum daily maintenance of CRR in two months. CRR is the slice of deposits that banks have to park with the RBI. This ratio is currently at 3 per cent. Resources deployed as CRR do not earn interest. V Rama Chandra Reddy, Head - Treasury, Karur Vysya Bank, said, “The RBI’s decision to restore the minimum daily CRR requirement to 90 per cent from 99 per cent, effective December 1, is a welcome relief for banks. It eases the tightrope in day-to-day CRR management, provides greater operational flexibility and helps moderate liquidity pressures.” “Interestingly, despite the tighter compliance requirement, banks have continued to maintain substantial SDF (Standing Deposit Facility) balances, reflecting the uneven distribution of liquidity and limited flexibility under the 99 per cent regime,” he added. He emphasised that while this move will not inject additional liquidity into the banking system, it will provide banks greater flexibility in managing CRR requirements and optimising funds, potentially resulting in lower SDF balances as they manage CRR requirements efficiently. K Arvind, Head - Treasury, Tamilnad Mercantile Bank, said, “This move provides some operational flexibility in maintaining daily CRR. articles.title: RBI rolls back tighter daily CRR requirement as banking liquidity slips into deficit

RBI rolls back tighter daily CRR requirement as banking liquidity slips into deficit | Stock Market News RBI forex interventions, liquidity absorption operations and government cash balances have tightened banking system liquidity. ( Reuters ) AI Quick Read Mumbai: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rolled back its recently tightened daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirement for banks as system liquidity slipped into deficit, with market participants expecting conditions to remain neutral or in deficit until March. In October, the RBI had raised the minimum daily CRR maintenance requirement to 99% from 90%, while keeping the overall CRR unchanged at 3%. CRR is the proportion of a bank’s deposits that it must maintain as cash with the central bank. The measure will take effect from 1 December, the central bank said in a statement on Friday. Banking system liquidity has tightened sharply, swinging from a surplus of nearly ₹ 11 trillion on 13 September to a deficit of ₹ 12,825 crore on 21 November, RBI data showed. The last time system liquidity was in deficit was on 22 June. As on 26 November, liquidity in the banking system was in a deficit of ₹ 47,641 crore. The squeeze has pushed up short-term borrowing costs, raising concerns that a prolonged increase in funding costs could weigh on economic growth. The tighter daily maintenance requirement was introduced to absorb surplus liquidity following substantial inflows through the foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposit scheme, which attracted $133 billion. With much of that liquidity now deployed by banks, market participants believe the need for the tighter requirement has diminished. Liquidity has been drained by multiple factors, including RBI’s foreign exchange market interventions, variable rate reserve repo (VRRR) auctions, open market operations (OMOs) and sell-buy swaps. The outlook for core liquidity, which adjusts system liquidity for the government’s cash balances, also points to a tightening of underlying liquidity conditions, said Gaura Sengupta, chief economist at IDFC FIRST Bank. The measure indicates the liquidity available to the banking system after accounting for funds held by the government with the RBI . “Once core liquidity starts coming down to around ₹ 4 trillion levels, you will be in a persistent system liquidity deficit situation,” Sengupta said. Government spending could temporarily push system liquidity into surplus in December, but she expects a persistent deficit in the fourth quarter as durable liquidity declines and government cash balances remain elevated. The liquidity squeeze is beginning to feed into short-term borrowing costs. Yields on three-month commercial papers issued by non-banking financial companies ( NBFCs ) rose by 80-83 basis points to 8.03-8.05% between 1 October and 25 November. Three-month Treasury bill yields also increased by 35-40 basis points to 5.85%, according to FBIL data. The weighted average call rate (WACR), the benchmark for overnight money market borrowing, is increasingly trading above the repo rate and closer to the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate, signalling tighter liquidity conditions, said VRC Reddy, treasury head at Karur Vysya Bank. “Corporate bond spreads are also widening. Spreads on AAA-rated public sector undertaking and non-banking financial company bonds have reached around 120-125 basis points over government securities, compared with the more normal range of 60-70 basis points, reflecting higher funding demand,” Reddy said. Since banking system liquidity slipped into deficit on 21 November, the RBI has conducted three variable rate repo (VRR) auctions, injecting nearly ₹ 1.75 trillion into the banking system. For now, market participants will be watching the RBI's monetary policy announcement on 4 December for signals on its liquidity stance. The liquidity squeeze also comes amid expectations of further monetary tightening. While a 25-basis-point rate hike at the December policy review is widely anticipated, a smaller section of the market sees the possibility of a larger 50-basis-point increase, depending on the inflation trajectory. Sengupta expects the RBI's calibrated tightening stance to continue, making a durable infusion of liquidity difficult to envisage. Higher borrowing costs, coupled with tighter liquidity, could eventually moderate credit growth as banks pass on increased funding costs to borrowers. The 31st meeting of the Standing Advisory Committee (SAC) to review the flow of credit to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) took place in Kolkata on November 27, 2026. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Deputy Governor Swaminathan J chaired the session, which focused on accelerating credit sanctions and reducing collateral dependence for small businesses. According to the RBI, the Deputy Governor recognised the role of MSMEs in India’s economy and development goals during the deliberations. He urged banks to speed up credit approvals and shift toward cash-flow-based lending through the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and other digital channels. The central bank official also called for wider adoption of the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) to support receivables financing. He emphasised the need for early identification and resolution of financial stress within the sector. Furthermore, the Deputy Governor invited industry associations to participate actively in outreach events. He specifically pointed to RBI town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings as platforms to raise awareness and bring member concerns directly to banks. The committee conducted a broad review of working capital and investment credit flowing to the sector. Members examined lending patterns for first-time borrowers and evaluated the extent of credit guarantee coverage. Deliberations also covered the higher limit set for collateral-free lending to micro and small enterprises. Participants discussed the settlement of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSE) invoices via TReDS alongside key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026. The meeting brought together senior government officials, including the Additional Secretary and Development Commissioner from the Ministry of MSME, and the Joint Secretary from the Department of Financial Services under the Ministry of Finance. Managing directors and executive directors of select banks attended the session in Kolkata. Heads of key financial and development institutions, including SIDBI, NABARD, CGTMSE, NCGTC, and KVIC, joined the discussions. The Chief Executive Officer of the Indian Banks’ Association and representatives from national, regional, and state-level MSME associations also participated in the review meeting. stories.brief: The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed exec with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair, is a Chinese spy.

articles.title: Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang
articles.text:
Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang | World News - Business Standard
Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang | World News - Business Standard Home / World News / Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang Nvidia's Blackwell chips found at China data centre linked to Alice Huang Regulatory filings reveal that Nvidia's advanced Blackwell chips were installed at a Shanghai data centre linked to Alice Huang and Megaspeed despite US export restrictions Bloomberg 8 min read Last Updated : Nov 27 2026 | 11:57 PM IST Listen to This Article A pair of Chinese firms installed Nvidia Corp’s powerful Blackwell semiconductors in a Shanghai data centre linked to Alice Huang, the woman at the heart of a controversy surrounding the US chipmaker. The gear installed at the Yangtze River Delta Project included a GB300 NVL72 rack, among Nvidia’s most powerful products, according to a serial number specified in documents submitted to Chinese regulators in November. Shanghai Shuoyao offered the hardware as collateral to obtain a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, according to filings from the lender that were reviewed by Bloomberg News. A second firm, Shanghai Kezhan, controlled by a Tokyo-based parent, described a GB200 server — which also relies on Blackwell chips — at the facility. That description was provided in documents when it obtained a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a finance-leasing firm wholly owned by a local Shanghai government agency. Nvidia shares fell as much as 2.6 per cent to $145.39 after markets opened in New York on Friday. The submissions reveal for the first time that Nvidia’s Blackwell processors found their way into a Chinese data centre that has ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed. These processors were until recently Nvidia’s most powerful data centre products, and they have always been illegal to ship to China without a US licence. Also Read SAP's global job cuts likely to affect nearly 1,000 employees in India premium Former Nvidia executive under scanner over sale of servers to China Who is Raul John Aju, the 'AI Kid of India' who met Russian Prez Putin? Nvidia chip sellers warn neoclouds against serving Chinese firms: Report Swiggy's Instamart lays off 340 employees amid wider AI adoption push President Donald Trump has explicitly said he doesn’t want these chips — which OpenAI and Anthropic PBC use to train their most cutting-edge models — going to the Asian country, at least for now. Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, meanwhile, once claimed they were too big to smuggle: a standard two-metre-tall GB300 NVL72 server rack, which contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips and 36 Grace processors, can weigh more than 1,500 kilograms (3,300 pounds) and is about the size of a gigantic fridge. Nvidia and its just-reinstated CEO have come under intense scrutiny in recent weeks for their failure to stop diversion of the company’s products to China, a shadow trade that US officials believe is worth billions of dollars. It’s unclear how the GB300 rack made its way to the country, to Shanghai Shuoyao or to this specific site — described in local media as designed to house as many as 800,000 servers. By inputting the serial number for the product into a public warranty database, Bloomberg found that it was manufactured by Taiwan’s Gigabyte Technology Co, which assembles Nvidia chips into servers and racks. The database also provided a model name for the serial number, which matches a GB300 NVL72 server rack manufactured by the Taiwanese company. This sort of gear often passes through several hands — including local distribution networks — before it’s installed in data centres. In many cases, products that were ultimately smuggled into China were originally sold to parties in unrestricted areas. Bloomberg provided the rack’s serial number to Gigabyte, seeking information about to whom Gigabyte had originally sold the hardware and when. It declined to answer those questions, citing company policy. The firm “conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations”, a spokesperson said in an emailed statement. “All transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time.” Shanghai Shuoyao — the company that procured the GB300 rack and offered it as collateral — is active at the data centre linked to Alice Huang and also has significant overlap with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under US investigation over concerns that it smuggled Nvidia chips to China, Bloomberg has reported. Shanghai Shuoyao, which hasn’t responded to Bloomberg queries over the past year, confirmed this month in a rare public statement that it is one of Megaspeed’s service providers, describing the partnership as “limited to ordinary commercial cooperation”. Megaspeed, meanwhile, used a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project in 2024 to describe its largest data centre to investors, dubbing the site a “specific area” facility in an unnamed country. Bloomberg does not have evidence that Megaspeed itself diverted Nvidia hardware there, and Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing in response to the US probe. The company has not answered repeated queries about the Yangtze River Delta Project. Nor has Nvidia, which for years insisted that there was no black market for its products and didn’t respond to questions for this story. The Trump administration this month put Megaspeed on a US trade blacklist, citing a significant risk of involvement in chip diversion. Alice Huang in 2023 founded Megaspeed, a so-called neocloud that won a coveted stamp of approval from Nvidia within four days of its creation, and went on to become the chipmaker’s largest Southeast Asian customer. She also has ties to a number of companies that invested in the Yangtze River Delta Project, which counts Kang Wei as its president. Kang has been introduced at times as Alice Huang’s romantic partner, people familiar with the matter said. It’s unclear how far along operators are in meeting their overall goal for that project, which at 800,000 servers would be on par with hyperscale facilities used by companies like OpenAI. It’s also unclear what mix of servers they plan to use. The parameters they’ve outlined in construction plans reviewed by Bloomberg — specifically, the total processing power as compared to the energy input — would be extremely difficult to satisfy with chips from Chinese companies such as Huawei Technologies Co. Still, the smuggled hardware disclosed in the filings reviewed by Bloomberg is just a fraction of what they’d need. These documents only cover hardware offered as collateral for loans — providing a small snapshot of the operators’ ambitions, while also underscoring how some Chinese financial institutions, including those with government ties, were aware that restricted hardware was getting into China and were willing to lend capital on those assets. Bloomberg was unable to reach either the leasing company that lent money to Shanghai Kezhan or Shanghai Innovation Bank, which, in addition to the money it lent Shanghai Shuoyao, also provided a 200 million yuan loan to another company called Shanghai Longjie, similarly with restricted Nvidia chips as collateral. Shanghai Longjie — which has the same parent company as Shanghai Shuoyao — disclosed in documents filed with regulators that it has servers containing Nvidia’s earlier Hopper-generation chips, which are illegal to ship to China without Washington’s permission, Bloomberg reported this month. That hardware was manufactured by Super Micro Computer Inc and Dell Technologies Inc. It’s unclear whether the shipments had US approval. Those aren’t the only Hopper chips at the Yangtze River Delta Project. Shanghai Kezhan, the company that described the GB200 server in filings last year, also disclosed that it has 32 servers with H200 chips there. These products had a Gigabyte prefix in their model name, but the documents didn’t include serial numbers — making them harder to trace. Shanghai Kezhan is headquartered about half a kilometre from the Yangtze River Delta Project, at the same commercial complex where Shanghai Shuoyao solicited engineers to work on Nvidia H100 and H200 chips — two restricted models. In February 2024, both of these firms added “imports and exports” to their business activities, according to data from Qizhidao, a company information provider. The same month, Megaspeed’s original parent — the Chinese gaming giant 7Road — obtained 16.7 per cent of Shanghai Kezhan via a subsidiary the gaming company bought from Alice Huang in 2019. The other 83.3 per cent of Kezhan is ultimately owned by NeXPower Japan, according to Qizhidao. Japan’s official companies registry returned only one company named NeXPower, which was established in March 2025. Caixin, a Chinese business news outlet, said the Tokyo firm is controlled by Alice Huang. Bloomberg has been unable to reach NeXPower for comment. Chinese-speaking staffers at the firm’s registered address wouldn’t confirm that it was NeXPower’s office, and shut the door after Bloomberg News asked about their relationship with Alice Huang and Shanghai Kezhan. On the intercom was a message saying they were working and would not respond to media questions. The registered address of the company’s director appeared to be a vacated residence. In May 2025, records compiled by Big Trade Data show, Shanghai Kezhan received a shipment worth $11 million, flown from Malaysia to Shanghai Pudong International Airport with the company as consignee. The customs document described the shipment as “storage chassis”, referring to a structure that houses components of a storage server. But the product code it was assigned to was 847150, which denotes computing servers. The shipment’s unit price was $264,108, too costly for a storage chassis — but within the price range of servers powered by Nvidia’s Hopper chips. Bloomberg traced the lineage of one GB300 server rack to Gigabyte Technology. Sean Gallup/Getty Images Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Well, this is awkward. As Bloomberg notes, Jensen Huang once claimed GB300 racks are too big to smuggle. It's unclear how the GB300 and GB200 units made their way to the Shanghai facility, which may eventually house as many as 800,000 servers. However, Bloomberg was able to partly track the lineage of the GB300 unit. By putting the serial of the rack into a public warranty database, the outlet was able to trace it back to Taiwan's Gigabyte Technology, which PC gamers will know as one of NVIDIA's many add-in board partners. Like other NVIDIA AIBs, Gigabyte buys GPU chips from the company that it then uses to manufacture graphics cards for consumers and servers for enterprise customers. Gigabyte declined to answer Bloomberg's questions about what company or party originally bought the GB300 rack. A spokesperson told the outlet it "conducts all business in compliance with applicable laws and regulations," adding, "all transactions are subject to our internal compliance requirements and the relevant laws and regulations in effect at the time." Shanghai Shuoyao, the company that offered a GB300 as collateral, has ties with Megaspeed. Alice Huang took a controlling stake in the Singaporean cloud computing company in 2023 before leaving it in August 2025. Earlier this month, Shanghai Shuoyao said it was one of Megaspeed's service providers, but described its relationship with the company as "limited to ordinary commercial cooperation." According to Bloomberg , Megaspeed used renderings of the Yangtze River Delta Project in a presentation it shared with investors in 2024. The deck did not list China as the location of the data center. Bloomberg notes it does not have evidence that Megaspeed directly diverted NVIDIA chips to the data center, and the company denies any wrongdoing . The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed broke US export rules . NVIDIA did not immediately respond to Engadget's comment request. Alice Huang appears to have had a number of other ties to the Yangtze River Delta Project. Most notably, through Kang Wei, the man The New York Times reports was often introduced as her husband and appears to have had ties with China's Ministry of State Security. Bloomberg found him listed as the president of the facility. The publication also found evidence of servers containing NVIDIA's earlier Hopper-generation chips inside the Yangtze River Delta Project. Those GPUs are also illegal to ship to China without permission from the US government. Jensen Huang is set to testify publicly before Congress on December 3 at 10AM ET.

articles.title: Is Alice Huang a spy or not?
articles.text:
Is Alice Huang a spy or not? | TechCrunch
Is Alice Huang a spy or not? Lucas Ropek 12:00 PM PST · November 26, 2026 The central, still-unproven claim in the Nvidia scandal is that Alice Huang, a former executive at the data-center company Megaspeed, is a Chinese spy. She had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging it and was just as abruptly reinstated on Monday of this week. What’s publicly known is murkier than the headlines suggest. U.S. intelligence has reportedly tracked Alice Huang’s contact with an officer of China’s spy agency, but officials haven’t offered public evidence that she was commissioned to target Nvidia’s chief. In the past week, after President Trump successfully pushed to bring Jensen Huang back, the administration has played down the allegations it once circulated internally. Whether that reflects new intelligence or political pressure is the big question. Undisputed reporting shows the claim emerged from the White House itself . It first appeared in a highly classified memo written in March under the oversight of Secretary of State Marco Rubio and circulated to White House officials ahead of Trump’s trip to China in May. The memo formed the partial basis for the New York Times’ initial reporting on the scandal, published Oct. 29 and its existence was first reported on Nov. 8 . The memo did not definitively say, according to the Wall Street Journal, that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. CNN, by contrast, has reported that the memo concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset. What’s better established is that Alice Huang was in touch with Chinese intelligence. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) is Beijing’s civilian spy agency, responsible for both foreign intelligence and domestic counterintelligence. Last weekend, the Times, citing people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports, reported that Huang was in contact with an MSS officer from the spring of 2025 until this fall , a period that overlaps her relationship with Jensen Huang. (The Chinese government has called the spy claims a “smear,” and Megaspeed says Huang left the company in August 2025 and that its business is legitimate.) Attorney General Todd Blanche, who was Trump’s personal defense lawyer before taking over the Justice Department, told journalists on Tuesday: “I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.” On the same day, Trump said a pardon was an option for Jensen Huang but that he did not think one would be needed. Senior intelligence officials reportedly told Congress that the government apparently has no actual evidence that the MSS directed Alice Huang to pursue an affair with Jensen Huang. None of those statements necessarily exonerates Alice Huang as an intelligence agent. Instead, they support the alternate theory that the Chinese government didn’t tell her to begin the affair and that Jensen Huang broke no law by having it. From a certain angle, the circumstantial evidence surrounding Alice Huang looks quite suspicious. She was a top executive at a company investigated for illicitly channeling Nvidia chips to China, and her husband, Kang Wei, is said to have even closer ties to the MSS, with some sources saying he worked for the agency. The timing of the government’s reversal is at the heart of the matter. Trump has said he lobbied the board “directly and indirectly” to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, so it wouldn’t be surprising if officials who serve at his pleasure were recasting the case in terms that satisfy his agenda. That wouldn’t necessarily make their assessments wrong. But unless new intelligence has actually resolved the question, and none has been publicly identified as yet, that backdrop is critical to keep in mind. CBS has also reported that Rubio has privately voiced concerns about aspects of Jensen Huang’s return. Earlier this month, CNN reported that the intelligence community was still working to understand Alice Huang’s relationship with Jensen Huang and that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove she was acting as a spy for Beijing. After a briefing by top intelligence officials earlier this month, Rep. Jim Himes (D-Conn.), the incoming chair of the House Intelligence Committee, said he was unsure whether she was a spy or a “ useful idiot .” And this week, the Wall Street Journal pointed out that under Chinese leader Xi Jinping, top corporate executives routinely maintain ties to the country’s intelligence service without being formally deputized as assets. The crush of conflicting claims, most from anonymous government sources, obviously leaves large questions unanswered as to what actually transpired. Some of those questions that naturally spring to mind: There are answers to all of these questions, of course, but when the public will get them is anybody’s guess. Jensen Huang is due to appear before the Senate Banking Committee next week, and by the look from the statements of some of its members , he’s likely in for a rough ride. Unfortunately, congressional hearings, particularly public ones, rarely unearth secrets that haven’t already been disclosed.
